name: Crossline
listed_description: A small, self-contained, zero-config, MIT licensed, cross-platform, readline and libedit replacement.
reason: README and repo page (160 stars, MIT, pure C, crossline.c/crossline.h plus examples and doc/) give only size comparisons (about 1200 lines of code versus libreadline's 30K+, linenoise about 1,100, linenoise-ng about 4,300) and feature comparisons. No speed benchmark and no numeric performance comparison against readline, libedit or linenoise anywhere reachable; also a line editor, not a lexer, so the guessed category was wrong.

name: csv2
listed_description: Fast CSV parser for modern C++.
reason: README benchmark (benchmark/main.cpp, g++ -O3 -std=c++11, Apple M1 Pro, 7 Kaggle datasets from 0.077 s for 111 MB to 3.026 s for 4 GB) times csv2 alone: mmap plus iterate every cell. benchmark/main.cpp contains no competitor, no std::getline loop and no other parser. No third-party shootout including csv2 was found (checked csv-parser's benchmarks/README.md, dfglib csvPerformanceRuns.md, MIOCSV, CSV_co READMEs and WebSearch). Issue #37 (benchmark cell count 7,762,529 vs 7,991,460 expected for Denver crime data) has no comparison either.

name: cxxopts
listed_description: Lightweight C++ command line option parser.
reason: Repo page (4.8k stars, MIT) and README make no performance, size or compile-time claims with numbers and no comparison against getopt or Boost.Program_options. WebSearch for compile-time, binary-size or speed comparisons of cxxopts, CLI11, Boost.Program_options and getopt returned only qualitative descriptions. Also an argument parser, not a parser generator, so the guessed category was off.

name: lazycsv
listed_description: A fast, lightweight and single-header csv parser for modern C++.
reason: Repo page (97 stars, MIT, 27 commits) has no benchmark directory; README says only that it is fast and lightweight and allocates nothing in the constructor or while parsing, with a performance note about re-parsing cost and no numbers. Issues page empty. No third-party shootout with numbers for it found (checked csv-parser benchmarks, dfglib runs and WebSearch; the lazycsv hits were an unrelated Python/Rust library).
